questions.question: Sri Lanka is separated from India by a narrow channel of sea formed by the Palk Strait and the ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the __**Gulf of Mannar**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Sri Lanka is separated from India by the Palk Strait and the Gulf of Mannar.
 
• It is situated between Tamil Nadu (India) and Jaffna district (Sri Lanka).
 
• The strait is named after the former governor of Madras, Robert Palk.
 
• The Palk Strait is bounded by
 
 
• Pamban Island (India)
 
• Adam's (RAM Setu) Bridge
 
• The Gulf of Mannar (Sri Lanka)
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/029465d520aa00c2200d82709b77402e73ddcb2fa9583730b791ae4ea014654a.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gulf of Strait**:

 
 
• A strait is a narrow body of water connecting two larger bodies of water, not a gulf.
 
• Famous straits include the Strait of Hormuz and Strait of Malacca, vital for international maritime routes.
 
• Straits are often strategically significant due to their location and role in global trade.
 
 
 
• **Gulf of Kutch:**
 
 
• Located on the west coast of India, in the state of Gujarat, bordering the Arabian Sea.
 
• Known for its tidal energy potential and the Rann of Kutch, a salt marsh area.
 
• It plays an important role in trade, with Kandla Port being one of India’s major seaports situated along its shores.
 
 
 
• **Gulf of Khambat (also known as Gulf of Cambay)**:
 
 
• Situated on the western coast of India in Gujarat, connecting to the Arabian Sea.
 
• Known for its high tidal range and strong tidal currents, making navigation difficult.
 
• Historically important for trade and commerce, with cities like Bharuch located along its shores.

questions.question: What is Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR)?

options.text: It's the percentage of deposits that banks must keep in liquid form in the short term
It's the interest rate at which banks borrow from the central bank
It's the ratio of government bonds to total assets held by a bank
It's the ratio of a bank's capital to its total assets

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It's the percentage of deposits that banks must keep in liquid form in the short term.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Statutory Liquidity Ratio refers to the percentage of a bank's net demand and time liabilities** (NDTL) that it must maintain in the form of specified liquid assets
 
• The **primary purpose of SLR **is to ensure the liquidity and solvency of banks.
 
• Thereby **SLR promotes the stability of the financial system**.
 
• SLR is mandated by the central bank of a country (for example, the Reserve Bank of India in India)
 
 
• to ensure that banks have sufficient liquidity to meet customer withdrawals and other obligations.
 
 
 
• The main objective of maintaining the SLR is to ensure the solvency and financial stability of banks and to prevent them from over-lending.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** Some important Banking Terms 

 
• CRR (Cash Reserve Ratio)

 
 
• The Cash Reserve Ratio is the percentage of a bank's net demand and time liabilities (NDTL) that must be maintained as cash reserves with the central bank (e.g., the Reserve Bank of India in India).
 
• **It ensures that banks have a minimum level of liquidity to safeguard customer deposits and manage liquidity risks**.
 
• A higher CRR reduces the amount of funds available for lending, while a lower CRR increases banks' ability to lend.
 
 
 
• **Repo Rate**
 
 
• The Repo Rate is the interest rate at which the central bank lends money to commercial banks in exchange for government securities.
 
• **It is used by central banks to control inflation and manage liquidity in the economy.**
 
• When the repo rate is high, borrowing becomes more expensive for banks, which can lead to higher interest rates for consumers.

questions.question: Which of the following five-year plan of India has achieved its target growth?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the__** Eighth Plan**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Eighth Five-Year Plan of India, which spanned from 1992 to 1997, achieved its target growth.
 
• This plan focused on the modernization of industries, improvement in technology, and infrastructure development.
 
• During this period, India liberalized its economy significantly and initiated several economic reforms aimed at reducing the control of the government on various aspects of the economy and promoting private sector participation.
 
• These reforms led to a substantial increase in economic growth and productivity.
 
• The target growth rate for the Eighth Plan was 5.6%, but India managed to achieve an average growth rate of around 6.8%, which was higher than the targeted rate.
 
• The success of the Eighth Plan can be attributed to the positive response to economic liberalization, increased foreign investments, and a general move towards a more market-oriented economy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Eleventh Plan (2007-2012**):

 
 
• Target Growth Rate: 9%
 
• Achieved Growth Rate: Approximately 8%
 
• The Eleventh Plan aimed at “faster and more inclusive growth.” During this period, India witnessed strong economic growth, yet it fell short of the targeted 9%.
 
• The global financial crisis of 2008-2009 significantly impacted India's economy, leading to lower growth than anticipated. Although sectors like services continued to perform well, issues such as inflation, infrastructural bottlenecks, and slower agricultural growth posed a challenge
 
 
 
• ​Ninth Five-Year Plan:
 
 
• Its duration was from 1997 to 2002, under the leadership of Atal Bihari Vajpayee. 
 
• The main focus of this plan was “Growth with Social Justice and Equality”.
 
• It was launched in the 50th year of independence of India.
 
• This plan failed to achieve the growth target of 6.5% and achieved a growth rate of 5.6%.
 
 
 
• Tenth Five Year Plan:
 
 
• Its duration was from 2002 to 2007, under the leadership of Atal Bihari Vajpayee and Manmohan Singh. 
 
• This plan aimed to double the Per Capita Income of India in the next 10 years.
 
• It also aimed to reduce the poverty ratio by 15% by 2012.
 
• Its growth target was 8.0% but it achieved only 7.6%.

questions.question: In India, the salaries of the Supreme Court judges are determined by ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the __**Parliament of India**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In India, **the salaries of the Supreme Court judges are determined by Parliament**
 
• **Article 125:** This article of the Constitution of India states that Parliament determines the salaries, allowances, and rights of Supreme Court judges. 
 
• Parliament **can decide the salaries through legislation.** 
 
• The salaries of **Supreme Court judges are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India**
 
• The salaries and allowances of the judges cannot be varied to their disadvantage after their appointment, except during a financial emergency.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Supreme Court -

 
 
• Its provision has been made under Part V (Union) and Chapter IV of the Indian Constitution.
 
• Articles 124 to 147 in Part V of the Constitution deal with the Supreme Court.
 
• The Constitution of India under Article 124(1) states that there shall be a Supreme Court of India consisting of a Chief Justice (CJI).
 
• and there may not be more than seven other judges unless Parliament by law determines a larger number of other judges.

questions.question: Which one is the Traditional Celebrations of Kerala?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Onam.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Onam is a traditional celebration of Kerala** that highlights the state's culture, tradition, and communal harmony
 
• Onam is** usually celebrated in August or September.**
 
• Onam is **rooted in the legend of King Mahabali **who visited Kerala during Onam
 
• It i**ncludes the famous Pookalam (flower rangolis), Vallamkali (boat races), Kathakali performances, traditional feasts (Onasadya), and various games.**
 
• It is a **10-day celebration**, with Thiruvonam being the most significant day.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nag Pancham**i

 
 
• It is a** Hindu festival dedicated to the worship of snakes, **particularly the Nagas (serpent deities).
 
• It is Celebrated on the fifth day of the bright half of the lunar month of Shravana (July/August).
 
• Devotees offer milk, flowers, and prayers to snake idols or live snakes to seek protection from snake bites and honour their role in Hindu mythology.
 
• The festival is rooted in the belief that snakes are divine beings, with references to them in ancient texts like the Mahabharata.
 
 
 
• **Hornbill Festival**
 
 
• It is ** Celebrated in Nagaland, India.**
 
• It is ** Known as the "Festival of Festivals,**" it showcases the rich cultural heritage of the Naga tribes.
 
• It features traditional music, dance, folk performances, crafts, games, and indigenous food, with highlights including the Naga Warrior Dance and Hornbill Rock Contest.
 
• It Promotes inter-tribal unity and celebrates the traditions of Nagaland while attracting tourists from across the globe.
 
 
 
• **Baisakhi**
 
 
• It is a** major Sikh festival marking the harvest season in Punjab**, and also commemorates the formation of the Khalsa in 1699 by Guru Gobind Singh.
 
• It is **Celebrated on April 13 or 14 every year.**
 
• The Sikhs visit gurdwaras, perform seva (selfless service), and participate in processions (nagar kirtans). Traditional dances like Bhangra and Gidda are performed.
 
• It Marks the beginning of the harvest season for the Rabi crops, especially wheat, in northern India.

questions.concept: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.question: What is the atomic number of Helium according to the modern periodic table?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** 2.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **atomic number of helium on the modern periodic table is 2.**
 
• Helium's **symbol is He**, and **it is a noble gas.**
 
• The atomic number of an element indicates the number of protons in its nucleus

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f82cd653d2fb62cbb7bcac927550d6c57a114f4cc5b6964efc3582e73e7aa85b.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **modern periodic table**:

 
 
• Elements in the modern periodic table are arranged in order of increasing atomic number (the number of protons in the nucleus), rather than atomic mass.
 
• The properties of elements are periodic functions of their atomic numbers, meaning elements with similar properties recur at regular intervals.
 
 
• This leads to the grouping of elements with similar chemical behaviours in vertical columns called groups.
 
 
 
• The table consists of **18 vertical columns** called *groups* and **7 horizontal rows** called *periods*.
 
• Elements in the same group have similar chemical properties due to having the same number of valence electrons.
 
• The modern periodic table is divided into four main blocks: s-block, p-block, d-block, and f-block, based on the electron configuration of the elements.
tags: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.question: Who among the following addressed World Parliament of Religions at Chicago in 1893?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Swami Vivekananda**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Swami Vivekananda** addressed the **World Parliament of Religions** at Chicago in **1893**.
 
• The World Parliament of Religions was held as part of the World's Columbian Exposition and
 
 
• aimed to promote interfaith dialogue and understanding among various religions.
 
 
 
• In his opening address, Swami Vivekananda introduced Hinduism to the Western world and spoke about universal acceptance and tolerance
 
 
• highlighting the importance of harmony among religions.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Raja Ram Mohan Roy:
 
 
• He was a prominent social and educational reformer in India during the early 19th century.
 
• He is best known for his efforts to abolish the practice of Sati and for founding the Brahmo Samaj.
 
 
 
• ​Swami Vivekananda:
 
 
• He was a key figure in the introduction of Indian philosophies of Vedanta and Yoga to the Western world.
 
• He is best known for his speech at the Parliament of the World's Religions in Chicago in 1893.
 
• His works primarily focused on spirituality and nationalism.
 
 
 
• **Swami Dayanand Saraswat**i
 
 
• He was a Hindu religious leader.
 
• He founded the Arya Samaj, a movement that aimed to reform Hinduism and promote Vedic teachings.
 
 
 
• **Ishwarchandra Vidyasagar**
 
 
• **​He **was a Bengali polymath.
 
• He worked towards women's education and social reforms in the 19th century.
